A rare genetic mutation called pseudo-melanism has resulted in roughly half of the tigers in India's Similipal Tiger Reserve sporting coats with far more black than those of usual tigers. This widespread coloration is a symptom of a shallow gene pool in a region that previously faced a dwindling tiger population, and could prove catastrophic if conservation officers aren't able to find these tigers more genetically diverse mates. This tiger became a powerful symbol of HOPE for tiger recovery in China, and she was named the ‘Hero Tigress’. 💚🐯 Hero Tigress’ first stepped into the mountain forests of Hunchun in 2019. Since then, she’s given birth to a total of thirteen cubs over four litters, making her one of the most prolific Amur tigers on record. This is even more remarkable if you consider that only around 30% of wild Amur tiger cubs are thought to survive to adulthood. And now, at least two of Hero’s daughters are having cubs of their own. 🥹 China’s wild Amur tiger population has grown to around 70 by 2025 (up from only 20 tigers in 2010).
